alex_customer: Hey team — we just got a bespoke SIG/CAIQ follow-up from our security team. They want a keystore export proof, HSM attestation artifacts, and audit-log slices for the last 13 months. Due date in their ticket is next Friday, and they hit us with a couple of 401s when trying to pull exports yesterday. Can you confirm what we can deliver and a safe repro path?

maya_cs: Thanks Alex — we can help. Can you DM the ticket link and the exact API request that produced the 401? Also need the customer org id and whether they used the UI export or the API export.

alex_customer: Ticket here: https://zendesk.redwood/example/INC-4827. They used the API export via POST /v1/admin/keystore/export. Sample request from their security team below. They got 401 after a few hours into the export:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/keystore/export -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"org_id":"org-azura","range":"2023-01-01/2024-12-31","include_hsm":true}'```

li_engineer: tagging in. 401 can be a few things: expired key, session TTL, or a permissions policy on the dedicated export endpoint. Can you paste the response body they saw? Also, did they use a customer-managed KMS key or our managed key for the HSM export?

alex_customer: Response was: ```{ "error": "unauthorized", "message": "invalid_api_key: token expired" }``` They said they rotated keys earlier this month and were using an SDK wrapper. They claim the key was valid for other endpoints. They also provided a partial log: `export: start -> 2024-11-03T12:00Z; progress: 40% -> 2024-11-03T12:08Z; error: 401 -> 2024-11-03T12:09Z`

maya_cs: Ok — two parallel tracks: (1) repro & fix the 401 with engineering, (2) prepare the compliance artifacts (attestation + logs). For artifacts we'll need to coordinate with security for attestation evidence and with infra for log slices.

li_engineer: Repro plan: ask them to (A) call `GET /v1/account/me` with same token immediately after export to validate token; (B) attach `X-Request-ID` header to export call so we can trace in logs; (C) if using SDK, ask them to disable auto-rotate to rule out middleware rotation. Example quick-check:```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxxx" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/me``` If that returns 200, token is ok. If not, we capture the 401 trace. I'll ask infra to trace request-id once they re-run with header.

owen_security: Important for attestation — we will need HSM firmware version, attestation cert chain, and an export manifest that indicates `include_hsm:true`. Also confirm data retention window they expect: SIG often asks for 13 months, but customer's policy here might be 24 months. Which retention window are they certifying?

alex_customer: Their compliance doc says 13 months. They also asked for proof that audit logs capture keystore access events with username, request-id, and result.

maya_cs: Understood. Owen — can security produce a template of what the attestation bundle should contain so we can ask infra to extract it? Also infra: can you produce a log slice for org-azura for 2023-01-01..2024-12-31 that includes `keystore.export` events and HSM access activity? Our standard export format is a gzipped JSONL with fields `{timestamp,event,request_id,actor,result}`.

audit-bot: Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/hsm-attestation-export contains the manifest checklist and required certificates. Also opened incident tracker RED-EXPORT-204 for manual export assistance.

li_engineer: Quick note on the 401: if their SDK rotated the token mid-export we might see partial export plus a 401. We do support resumable exports but only when the same API key session continues. For now propose: (1) Ask them to re-run export with non-rotating key and `X-Request-ID: org-azura-exp-<timestamp>`; (2) once they attach that header we can slice logs and, if necessary, resume/complete the export server-side for them. I can run a server-side resume with infra if they share the request-id and we confirm integrity.

owen_security: Confirming attestation items. I'll generate the attestation bundle template and sign-off note. I need the exact export manifest the customer expects (fields + hashing algorithm). If they need signed evidence (HSM signed manifest), that's more involved — we can provide an HSM-signed manifest if their workflow requires.

alex_customer: They want the manifest with sha256 of exported blobs and an HSM signature if possible. They're ok with a short delay, but want us to promise delivery before next Friday, which is 9 days out.

maya_cs: Proposed timeline:
- Today: gather logs about the 401, ask customer to re-run with headers (owner: li_engineer)
- +48h: infra produces log slice and raw export artifacts (owner: eng-infra)
- +72h: security produces attestation bundle template + HSM cert chain (owner: owen_security)
- Day 7: final signed manifest and gzipped export delivered to customer via secure transfer (owner: maya_cs)

li_engineer: I'll own the repro and flag infra for manual resume if they give request-id. Sending DM to alex_customer for the SDK wrapper stack trace.

alex_customer: DM replied with stack trace and SDK version. I'll have them re-run with the `X-Request-ID` in 30 mins.

maya_cs: Great — please upload the request-id and any response bodies into the Zendesk ticket. I'll update the ticket and the customer with the timeline above and escalate to account exec.

nowen_security: One last ask — for audit purposes, please confirm whether the customer used a customer-managed KMS key for the HSM export. If they did, we must include the customer KMS key identifier in the manifest.

alex_customer: They used our managed key.

maya_cs: Thanks — noting that. I'll set the delivery milestone in the ticket and ping the infra on-call. If anything blocks the HSM-signed manifest we'll provide a signed attest + explanation and escalate to legal if required. :thumbsup:
